headlines.title: CHP arrests suspect in connection with Bay Bridge freeway shooting
headlines.description: A California Highway Patrol investigation has identified two suspects and led to the arrest of one in connection with a freeway shooting that injured a passenger, authorities announced Monday. On Sept. 26, CHP officers responded to a shooting on eastbound Interstate 80 west of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge toll plaza, according to the agency. Investigators determined the shooting appeared targeted and retaliatory, stemming from an earlier physical altercation in San Francisco. According to authorities, the suspects allegedly followed the victims onto the freeway after the altercation and opened fire on their vehicle, striking a passenger in the leg. Investigators with the CHP Golden Gate Division Major Crimes Unit identified the suspects as 19-year-old Olman Santiago Martinezaguilar of San Pablo and a 15-year-old boy from Richmond. At about 6:15 a.m. Oct. 8, the CHP Golden Gate Division Warrant Service Team executed search and arrest warrants at residences in Richmond and San Pablo. Officers arrested Martinezaguilar at his San Pablo residence and recovered a firearm they believe is associated with him. The juvenile suspect was already in custody on an unrelated matter. Authorities booked Martinezaguilar into Santa Rita Jail on charges related to attempted murder, shooting at an occupied vehicle, and other offenses. “As California’s state police, the CHP is committed to protecting the public and holding people accountable for violence that endangers our communities,” said CHP Golden Gate Division Chief Steve Ramos. “This arrest reflects our investigators’ dedication to identifying those responsible and keeping Californians safe.”

headlines.title: San Francisco Firefighters rescue person from cliffside at Mile Rock Beach
headlines.description: San Francisco firefighters rescued one person from a rocky cliffside at Mile Rock Beach on Monday after deploying land and water resources, authorities said. The San Francisco Fire Department responded to multiple reports of individuals requiring rescue just before 3 p.m. Monday, according to the department. SFFD launched both land- and water-based rescue operations, locating the person from the land side as first-arriving crews set up for a rope rescue. Rescue Boat 35 and Rescue Boat 35A arrived on the scene and deployed rescue swimmers, who made contact with the stranded individual along the broken shoreline below a protected cliff off the Coastal Trail. Ground crews and rescue boat swimmers, alongside SFFD paramedics, reached the individual and assisted them back up the cliffside to the Coastal Trail for medical evaluation. Authorities confirmed that one individual was rescued by firefighters, while a second person declined assistance. Following the incident, the fire department issued a safety reminder urging the public to: — Stay on designated trails and never go off-trail; — Never turn your back on the ocean; — Always adhere to signage and use only designated access points.

headlines.title: Man flees SF police on scooter, killed after crashing into bus shelter
headlines.description: A police chase involving a man on an electric scooter ended in a fatal crash Monday in downtown San Francisco, leaving a toppled scooter, a backpack and a shattered scene at a bus stop shelter. The crash happened at the corner of Mission and Eighth streets. According to San Francisco police, officers attempted to serve an arrest warrant before the man raced away on an electric scooter, triggering a police pursuit. One witness, who asked to remain anonymous, described how the chase ended in Spanish, explaining that the man fell off the scooter and hit the bus shelter head-first. “Se bajo del scooter porque se kaio pegado en la parada esta de la ocho con su cabeza,” the witness said. A police officer who was running after the man also tripped during the pursuit, though the officer did not appear to suffer any serious injuries. Another witness, Maurice Navarro, described a disturbing scene as emergency crews attempted to save the man. “When I got here we had a CPR machine on the dude’s chest, limp body. Blood, hella blood all over the scene,” Navarro said. According to the witness who saw the end of the chase, the officers running after the man did not catch up to him until after he fell off and slammed into the bus stop. Police said the man was rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The department has not released any details regarding the arrest warrant they were attempting to serve. Traffic on Mission Street remained closed for hours as investigators collected evidence and worked to piece together the sequence of events.

headlines.title: Prop G brings fight over Great Highway and Sunset Dunes back to San Francisco voters
headlines.description: This upcoming Election Day will be something of a déjà vu for San Francisco voters, who for the second time will be asked to decide the future of the Great Highway and Sunset Dunes Park, through Proposition G. The ballot measure was crafted by opponents of the voter-approved Proposition K in 2024 that permanently closed a section of the Great Highway and allowed the new Sunset Dunes Park to operate full time. Prop G would reopen the Great Highway to cars during the week and allow it to be used as a park on weekends and holidays. It would be similar to how the roadway and park functioned before the passage of Prop K. “We’re simply saying, ‘Well, let’s share it,’” said Richard Correia, a retired San Francisco police commander who lives in the neighborhood and is part of the Prop G campaign. “Let’s share it during the week when people need to get around, and on the weekends and holidays, lets recreate here.” The park, which runs two miles along Ocean Beach, officially opened full time in April 2025. The Parks and Recreation Department said it attracts about 1.7 million people a year — although opponents believe that number is overinflated. The passage of Prop K was so controversial in San Francisco’s western neighborhoods that residents voted to recall Supervisor Joel Engardio for supporting it. But supporters of the park said it has been a huge success since its opening — drawing thousands of people to skate, bike, walk, jog and play on the roadway that fronts the beach and ocean. Since the park went full time, artists have added new installations and the park recently celebrated the opening of Shipwreck Cove, a play area for kids that resembles a shipwreck. The new Shipwreck Cove children’s playground sits on Sunset Dunes Park. It would have to be removed if Proposition G reopens the roadway to cars during the week. “It has been amazing just to see the community and the city make this space their own,” said Heidi Moseson, a member of Friends of Sunset Dunes who campaigned for Prop K. “If Prop G passes, park amenities like this amazing new playground behind me would have to get ripped out.” Critics of the park said the partial closure of the Great Highway between Lincoln Way and Sloat Boulevard has forced 18,000 cars a day onto residential streets. According to Corriea, it has slowed response times for emergency vehicles, led to more car crashes and has impacted the neighborhood’s quality of life. “You can’t squeeze 15,000 to 20,000 cars a day and squeeze them into a neighborhood without impacts,” Correia said. But Moseson disputed that assessment, saying nearby Sunset Boulevard has been able to pick up the slack for the re-routed traffic. “We had a lot of traffic engineers and examples from other places telling us, ‘Actually, we think the nearby Sunset Boulevard six-lane road can handle it,’” Moseson said. “And we’ve seen it can handle it.” Parks and Rec has estimated it will cost $10 million to return the park to a roadway, which includes reinstalling traffic lights. Some park features such as the playground would have to be removed as any amenities would have to be cleared from the roadway during the week to make way for cars. Visitors recreate at San Francisco’s Sunset Dunes Park during a recent weekday. The park’s future will be decided with Proposition G, which seeks to reopen the road to cars during the week. On a day last week, Sunset resident Megan Oxford wheeled her two children down the roadway of Sunset Dunes, a daily routine they’ve undertaken since the park opened. “I get it probably hurts some people,” Oxford said. “But we love that it’s closed to the cars and we can use it to play on and commute on our walk.” Park critic Albert Chow, owner of Great Wall Hardware and president of People of Parkside Sunset, said the park is underutilized during the week and doesn’t justify replacing a busy roadway. He said the closure has routed thousands of cars onto streets that never experienced much traffic. “It’s not that crowded on the weekdays, and when it’s foggy, cold and windy, there’s not that many people out there,” Chow said. “But 17,000 cars use that road every day, rain or shine.” Moseson said park visits are on the rise, and weekday visits now account for 60% of its usage. “I know change is hard,” Moseson said. “I think given that this road has lost its utility as a road, it’s now a great park, so let’s move forward and keep making it a great park.” Correia said the park, which is surrounded by the beach and Golden Gate Park, is too heavy a burden on the neighborhood’s commuters. “Why would you need to close a highway adjacent to the largest open space in San Francisco?” Correia said. “It doesn’t make any sense.” The new Shipwreck Cove children’s playground sits on Sunset Dunes Park. The return of the issue to the ballot in San Francisco is reminiscent of the fight over the Central Freeway, which was badly damaged in the 1989 Loma Prieta Earthquake. City voters elected to retain the freeway, which instructed Caltrans to begin its restoration. But critics went back to the ballot and a second vote resulted in voters approving its demolition. A glance around the Sunset neighborhood tells the story of the mixed feelings — with homes bearing “No On Prop G” signs sitting next to homes displaying signs reading “Open the Great Highway.” Whatever happens on Election Day, the park will remain — at least in some form, while some bitter feelings in a divided neighborhood are also likely to stick around. Elections Sep 17 Decision 2026 Oct 2

headlines.title: Bay Area celebrates Indigenous Peoples' Day
headlines.description: People across the Bay Area came together Monday to celebrate Indigenous Peoples’ Day. In the South Bay, several gathered at Santa Clara University where there was a renewed call to preserve the culture of the Bay Area’s Indigenous people. NBC Bay Area’s Marianne Favro takes a closer look and has more in her video report above. Pope Leo XIV Nov 15, 2025 Native Americans Oct 13, 2025 What is Indigenous Peoples Day? A day of celebration, protest and reclaiming history

headlines.title: Authorities identify 29-year-old woman killed in Oakland shooting
headlines.description: A 29-year-old Richmond woman was identified as the victim of a deadly shooting in downtown Oakland early Sunday morning. Mackayla “Kash” Paige was shot and killed shortly after 1:30 a.m. in the 200 block of 14th Street, according to police. Responding officers provided aid to Paige before she was taken to a hospital, where she later died. Officers arrested a Richmond woman in connection with the shooting, police said. Investigators believe she opened fire after getting into an argument with other people on the sidewalk. Homicide detectives have taken over the investigation and are looking into the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Additional information wasn’t immediately available.

headlines.title: San Jose police fatally shoot suspect who ‘brandished a firearm at officers'
headlines.description: San Jose police shot and killed a suspect who they say flashed a gun at officers, the department said Monday. The shooting happened late Sunday night along the 3000 block of Locke Drive in South San Jose, police said. Officers opened fire after the suspect brandished a firearm at them, police said. The suspect died at the scene. Police have not disclosed why officers were initially responding to the area. Neighbors who spoke to NBC Bay Area on Monday did not know what caused the confrontation, but said they saw a SWAT team and then heard gunshots. Some neighbors said the person who they believe was shot by police was someone who often acted erratically and would get upset when people came on his property. Police have not confirmed any details about the suspect. An investigation is ongoing and police may hold a news briefing on Tuesday to provide updates. headlines.title: 3,156-pound pumpkin grown in Rhode Island is inspected for possible world record
headlines.description: A Rhode Island pumpkin grower appears to have broken the world record for the heaviest pumpkin, with his giant squash topping the current record by nearly 300 pounds (136 kilograms). Ron Wallace of Greene, Rhode Island, weighed his pumpkin Saturday at a contest in New England and is now waiting for the Guinness Book of World Records to confirm he smashed the record, set about a week earlier by a grower in England. Wallace said he’s been in contact with Guinness officials who say his record is on track to be verified. “It’s truly massive, it was a pleasure to grow,” Wallace said Monday by phone. The Guinness Book of World Records currently lists a 2,857-pound (1,296-kilogram) squash grown by Ian Paton, of Lymington, England, as the record holder, set on Oct. 3. Guinness officials did not respond to a request for comment. The record-breaking gourd comes as growers across the world are joining competitions this month in the hopes their pumpkins will be crowned king. In Northern California on Monday, a Minnesota grower won a prominent annual competition for the fifth time in a row. Potential record-breaking pumpkin Wallace went home with $3,500 at his local contest. He said other competitions tried to entice him with bigger prize money, some totaling $70,000, but it was important for him to be surrounded by his hometown for the record-setting win. “I was just ecstatic, the place just exploded,” Wallace said, describing the moment the pumpkin was weighed. Wallace says he owes a lot to the pumpkin-growing community who always freely share tips and tricks to grow the biggest gourd. For the first time this year, Wallace began growing his pumpkins in a greenhouse, which he says makes a big difference. “The only way you create a 3,000-pound pumpkin is a community working together,” he said. Wallace got into the hobby after starting his own business selling gardening supplies online. He’s proud to be a part of the pumpkin-growing community and says competitions help legitimize growers. According to Wallace, the agriculture industry is increasingly reaching out to pumpkin-growers, asking for advice on soil and other growing techniques. The California pumpkin weigh-off is in its sixth decade In Northern California, a pumpkin named Rocky won a major annual pumpkin-weighing contest, tipping the scale at 2,389 pounds (1,083 kilograms), but fell far short of a possible new world record. Horticulture teacher Travis Gienger hauled his pumpkin across the country from Minnesota to win the contest for a fifth time. He’s going home with $21,501 in prize money after beating dozens of other giant pumpkin-growers in Half Moon Bay, south of San Francisco. He missed out on last year’s contest because his pumpkin broke while growing. Hoping for a comeback story, he named this year’s pumpkin “Rocky” after the iconic boxer played by Sylvester Stallone. “Five-time champion, that’s what we came here to do,” Gienger said following the win. Gienger and his family drove 35 hours, lugging a pumpkin the size of a small car, to California. Gienger grows his gourds in his backyard pumpkin patch in Anoka, a city on the banks of the Mississippi River north of Minneapolis, according to Ronan Fowler, the competition’s organizer. This year, Gienger had to deal with temperatures that dipped below freezing, and he says that in order to start competing more seriously, he’ll likely have to start growing pumpkins in a climate-controlled environment like Wallace. “The fact that Travis can weather the elements, like 30-degree weather, and still grow this massive pumpkin is pretty unbelievable,” Fowler said. Hundreds attended the 53rd World Championship Pumpkin Weigh-Off to enjoy food trucks, music, and pumpkin-related jokes. Earlier in the day, the crowd went wild when a very symmetrical pumpkin named Tinkerbell won the prettiest pumpkin contest. The prize money was calculated at $9 per pound of pumpkin, and Gienger’s winning gourd will be showcased during a parade through Half Moon Bay this weekend. Gienger missed out on an extra prize of $30,000 for breaking the world record. Sadly, these giants are grown for their size, not flavor, so there were no giant pumpkin pies at the end of the festival. ___ Associated Press writer Olga R. Rodriguez in San Francisco contributed to this report.
headlines.source: Terry Chea | The Associated Press and Mikella Schuettler | The Associated Press

headlines.title: WNBA Finals: Valkyries vs. Dream face arena challenges when series shifts to Atlanta
headlines.description: The Atlanta Dream will be hosting two games of the WNBA Finals next week, but it’s still not known where those contests will be played. The Dream, who face the Golden State Valkyries in the best-of-seven series that begins Saturday, will host Games 3 and 4 on Oct. 22 and 24. Atlanta would love to play those games at State Farm Arena, where the Hawks play, because it seats over 17,000 fans. But that site isn’t available because of a concert by singer Sombr the same night as Game 3 and the Hawks have their home opener the evening of Game 4. With a 12:30 p.m. PST start for Game 4, there wouldn’t be enough time to get the arena ready for the Hawks game. If the WNBA Finals go to six games, State Farm Arena also isn’t available for Game 6 on Oct. 29 as the Hawks have another home contest that evening. WNBA 17 hours ago San Francisco Oct 9 Breaking News Oct 9 The Dream played most of their regular season games at Gateway Center Arena which holds only 3,500 fans. Atlanta moved six regular season games and the three previous home playoff games to State Farm Arena. Atlanta will play all its games next season at State Farm Arena after signing a multi-year deal earlier this month. Last week Dream president and chief operating officer Morgan Shaw Parker said the team was “finalizing details on their home venue and where we will be playing” for the Finals. If the games can’t be moved, it wouldn’t be the first time that the league it championship games in a smaller venue. The Washington Mystics hosted three games in the 2019 WNBA Finals in their home, which seats just over 4,000 fans. There are other bigger facilities in Atlanta that the Dream could potentially play in such as Georgia Tech or Gas South Arena — site of the ACC Tournament last year. The Dream hosted a Finals game there in 2013. The Valkyries had their own conflict with Game 2 on Oct. 19 as Doja Cat had a concert that night at Chase Center. The concert was moved to Oct. 25.

headlines.title: Search continues for hit-and-run driver who struck teen bike rider in Hayward
headlines.description: A 15-year-old boy is asking for the public’s help in finding the driver who struck him while he was riding a bike in Hayward last month. Jefferson Pineda was seriously injured at about 7:20 p.m. on Sept. 14 while riding an e-bike at the intersection of Alice and B streets near the Hayward BART station. Police said the driver ran a stop sign, struck Pineda and didn’t stop. Pineda broke several bones and is still recovering from head and leg injuries. Pineda and his family have been asking residents if their cameras captured the collision or images of the hit-and-run suspect. “Face up, be a man or something,” Pineda said. “You hit a kid. How are you going to hit a kid and just leave him there? What if he dies or something? What if I would’ve died? I don’t want to ride ever again, to be honest.” Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact Hayward police.

headlines.title: Woman dies after shooting in downtown Oakland
headlines.description: A woman died following a shooting in Oakland on early Sunday morning, according to the coroner’s office. The shooting occurred in the area of Harrison and 14th streets around 1:35 a.m., the Oakland Fire Department said. According to a report from The Mercury News, police said the woman got into a confrontation before someone shot her. The Oakland Fire Department confirmed the woman was transported by ambulance to a hospital. The coroner’s office confirmed that one person died from the shooting, and the police department later stated it was the woman who had been wounded. The police department said a woman from Richmond was arrested in connection with the incident. It has not yet been disclosed what sparked the alleged confrontation. The victim is not from Oakland, but police have not released her hometown or why she was visiting the city, The Mercury News reports.

headlines.title: Alysa Liu honored at Asian Health Service's Annual Gala in Oakland
headlines.description: The Bay Area’s golden girl Alysa Liu was honored at Asian Health Service’s Annual Gala in Oakland Saturday night. Liu made an incredible comeback at the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics. After winning gold, she said in August she’s taking a break from competition for a year. “For me, I kind of like to be 100 in something and because I have so many commitments this year, unforeseen commitments and stuff like that, and I want to explore all of them and I don’t like to split my energy and time because it doesn’t fulfill me as much,” Liu said. “So I’m going to do this stuff now and then go back to my regular skating routine next year.” The Asian Health Services is a health center nationally recognized for its advocacy work on behalf of patients for more than 50 years. “I think it’s really important because we are such an underserved community and the fact that there’s resources is so helpful,” Liu said. 2026 Milan Cortina Olympics Jan 9 Oakland Mar 12 The organization is located in the city’s Chinatown, a community Liu said helped shape her. “The Oakland Chinatown community is so important to me. It literally raised me and there’s so many incredible people here,” Liu said. “There’s really good food, there’s really good shops and the community here is really strong. And I love that we help each other.” The Team USA Figure Skating Champion was among three honorees that also included Shannon Lee, the daughter of Bruce Lee, and Hudson Yang, an actor, chef and mental health advocate.
